new_statements.rule_in_words: Yadu (Ronghong) Qiang is non-tonal and has word stress, which the authors mark throughout (departing from LaPolla & Huang 2003, following J. Sun 2003). In directional-prefix + verb-root words stress falls on the root (ti-'le, tu-'phu, tə-'dza), i.e. prefix unstressed; if the root vowel is schwa, stress retracts to the prefix ('tə-lə 'face'). Stress placement is vowel-quality sensitive: schwa is stressable only when the other vowels are schwa or /o/, and /o/ is never stressed (it surfaces as /u/ under stress). Unstressed vowels reduce to schwa, devoice or delete (final open syllables; after a stressed syllable in reduplication), and the vowel grades a ~ ɑ ~ ə suggest three degrees of stress. No general rule for all word types is given; the authors say the details of stress are for further study.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not treated as such; the authors infer 'three levels of stress' from three vowel grades (full /a/ or /ɑ/, schwa, deletion) in LaPolla & Huang's examples 'before/after it got dark' and 'become/still short' (p.175), without stating where a secondary stress falls.
new_statements.exceptions: Root vowel schwa -> stress retracts to the initial (prefix) syllable ('tə-lə, 'nə-lə, 'sə-lə 'face'); /o/ never stressed; schwa deletes in unstressed final open syllables and after a stressed syllable under reduplication (['nəllɑ] 'exchanged', ['tətʂtʂhə] 'weighed'); scope of the placement statement is DIR-prefixed verbs only.
new_statements.identity_note: All three works describe the same idiolect/variety: the speech of co-author Chenglong Huang, Ronghong village (c. 100 inhabitants), Yadu township, Chibusu district, Mao county, Aba Prefecture, Sichuan = the Ronghong variety of Yadu (Northern) Qiang, glottocode nort2722. Sims 2020 treats Ronghong only as the non-tonal northern comparandum (forms from LaPolla with Huang 2003); its own data are Yonghe and southern tonal varieties (qxs).

new_statements.relation_note: Agrees with the catalog record in type (Ronghong/Yadu = non-tonal northern Rma variety with word stress) and cites the very pages the catalog quotes (LaPolla with Huang 2003:33-35); adds nothing on placement, so the catalog classification undetermined is untouched by it. the compilers abstract-only classification ('says nothing about word stress in the Ronghong/Yadu variety') is superseded only to this extent: the body does make a type statement for the northern varieties.
new_statements.rule_in_words: A diachronic paper on proto-Rma tone. For the northern varieties, to which the Ronghong (Yadu) variety belongs and which it uses as its non-tonal comparandum, it states only the prosodic TYPE: no lexical tone, 'lexical stress-accent', citing LaPolla with Huang 2003:33-35 among others; it gives no rule for where stress falls, notes that the major northern descriptions do not mark stress-accent, and speculates that northern accent may continue an earlier culminative tone. Placement is therefore not determinable from this source (reading 'unclear' = type-only statement, no contradiction).
new_statements.exceptions: none for Ronghong; the paper's data tables cite Ronghong forms from LaPolla with Huang 2003 without stress marks.

readall_conflicts: No source contradicts the catalog record, whose kind is 'undetermined'. All three sources (LaPolla & Huang 2003 in the catalog, Evans & Huang 2007, Sims 2020) agree that Ronghong Yadu Qiang is non-tonal with word stress and stress-conditioned vowel reduction. The one tension is about default placement in prefixed verbs: LaPolla & Huang 2003:33 say 'In general there is a trochaic pattern of stress' (with the continuative prefix always stressed and derived forms varying by syllable count/type), while Evans & Huang 2007:174, who re-mark stress following J. Sun 2003, give DIR-prefix + root verbs as root-stressed (ti-'le, tu-'phu, tə-'dza) with retraction to the prefix only when the root vowel is schwa; LaPolla & Huang's own tə-wɑ́tsi 'become short' shows the same root stress, so the difference is one of generalisation rather than data. Neither work states a rule covering all word types and both defer the details of stress to further study; Sims 2020 states type only.
